_comment: Everything a human wrote and may want to change, in one place.
The split matters: this file is WRITTEN, the data.json files next to it are
COMPUTED by the pipelines in analysis/. Never hand-edit those — analysis/verify.py
will catch it. This file, on the other hand, is yours: edit it, commit, done.
You can edit it straight from github.com in the browser. No build step to run
//url: The canonical origin. Used for sitemap.xml, robots.txt and share-preview URLs, all of which need an absolute address. A wrong value here does not break the site, it just points crawlers at the wrong host.
//feed: The feed at /feed.xml. One entry per piece, newest first.
`published` is the date a piece went up. It is written here rather than
derived from anything because no date for it exists in the data — the
`retrieved` field in each data.json is the day the dataset was fetched,
which is not the day the writing was published, and the two must not be
confused. These came from the commits that added each piece.
A piece with no date here fails the build rather than going out of the
feed quietly. Add the line when you add the piece.

index.lede: Open data, followed all the way down to one person inside it.
index.blurb: Every piece here starts with a public dataset and ends with a story. The numbers can be checked: any figure set in mono opens its own evidence in a column to the right, so you never have to leave the sentence you are reading to find out whether it is true.

contact.lede: A portfolio of data analysis and narrative writing. Open to work that demands both at once.
contact.colophon: Analysis: Python, stdlib. Site: Next.js, static export. No backend and no database — the data changes at human speed, not machine speed, and every figure was computed before the page was built. The column structure is not a style: it is the argument. The prose sits in one column, its evidence opens in the next, and the trail you followed to check a number stays visible along the left edge.

//nav: An entry has either `pane` (opens a pane in the stack) or `href` (leaves the site).
